newsitem.title: UK: Man sees EU seen producing less sugar in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Man sees EU seen producing less sugar in 1996/97.

text.p: The European Union (EU) should produce 15.29 million tonnes of sugar in white value terms from its 1996/97 beet crop, down almost 374,000 tonnes on last year, international trade house E D & F Man said on Friday. In its August monthly report, Man said cold and dry spring weather in northern Europe caused delays in early beet development and summer drought had also dampened expectations.
Key producers France and Germany were both forecast to produce 3.95 million tonnes of sugar, but the French output would be lower than in 1995 and the German higher, it said.
Germany's beet crop seemed to have taken advantage of the late August rainfall and ensuing sunshine while the last French beet test showed a trend for the worse, the Man report said.

In Eastern Europe total 1996/97 sugar production was also expected to fall and would amount to 8.66 million tonnes, down 289,000 tonnes on the previous year, mainly as a result of lower Ukrainian and Russian outputs.

Ukraine was estimated to produce three million tonnes of sugar and Russia 1.9 million tonnes, it said. But Poland should buck the trend and produce 1.95 million tonnes, compared with 1.57 million last year. Elsewhere in the region, the forecast for other western European nations was put at 2.2 million tonnes, up from 1.8 million in 1995/96, mainly as a result of an increase in Turkey.
Beet tests in Switzerland appeared to indicate a big jump in yields and the country was forecast to produce 162,000 tonnes of sugar, Man said.
